players.product: Nebula autonomous lab, RAC robotics, and Ginkgo Datapoints

quarterly_data.signal: CFO Steven Coen: the divestiture of Biosecurity closed on April 3 and Biosecurity is now classified as discontinued operations, with all prior periods recast; Ginkgo now operates as a single segment and its financial commentary covers continuing operations only. H1 2026 revenue was $40 million, down 49%; excluding the $7.5 million of noncash revenue in H1 2025 from the mutual termination of the BiomEdit agreement, H1 revenue was down approximately 42%.
quarterly_data.figure: Biosecurity divestiture closed April 3; H1 2026 revenue $40 million (-49%; approximately -42% excluding $7.5 million BiomEdit noncash revenue)

quarterly_data.signal: CEO Jason Kelly on ADME-One validation: Ginkgo validated its five Tier 1 ADME assays with internal QC and by sending the same samples to external vendors, reporting good agreement in rank order (Spearman coefficient) and low / medium / high binning for kinetic solubility, permeability, human microsomal stability, P450 inhibition and plasma protein binding. It also tested the LOPAC small-molecule library (320 compounds) across three of its Tier 1 assays and published the dataset online. For ADME-One, Ginkgo partnered with Inductive Bio and Tangible Scientific to handle PK projection and compound management. CEO: 'We think we stand up very well to WuXi in terms of technical capability and throughput and we beat them on price.'
quarterly_data.figure: five Tier 1 assays validated against external vendors; LOPAC library 320 compounds across three Tier 1 assays
quarterly_data.counterparty_role: partner (with Tangible Scientific, handles PK projection and compound management for ADME-One)
